Title: Head injuries major preventable cause of death and disability

NewsContent:
"In last 20 years, due to increased number of automobiles on the road, number of road traffic accidents have increased manifolds and will continue to multiply", revealed Dr Naim-Ur- Rehman, Professor and Chief of Neurosurgery of the Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH). He was giving a presentation on "Head Injuries" at "Signs, Symptoms and Care", a monthly public health awareness program, held on May 29, 1999 at AKUH. Dr Rehman added that, "infant two- third of the people who die as a result of traffic accidents, die from head injuries". 

Labelling head injuries amongst the commonest causes of death and disability in traffic related accidents in Pakistan, Dr Rehman explained that head injuries are no respectors of geography and occur on open highways and far-flung places, which make all the more difficult to provide timely medical attention by a qualified neurosurgeon. Dr Rehman highlighted that timely and efficient care in the initial few hours ofthe injury can significantly reduce the number of fatalities and disability associated with these serious injuries. He further stressed that dissemination of road traffic accidents, fights, falls and bullets which are responsible for death and disability in large number of patients.

A panel of Neurology and Neurosurgery Consultants also participated in the panel discussion, which included Dr Shahid Masud Baig and Dr Ahmed Ali Shah.
